why: The gNB <-> broker <-> UE chain is lock-step: every slot waits one full round of thread handoffs. On a big.LITTLE host with deep idle states, handoffs that land on little cores or wake a core from its deepest idle state push the round past the slot period. Pinning the three processes to separate big-core sets is what brought 100 MHz on GB10 from 0.72x to real time (SPARK_MILESTONES.md S10).

spark-gb10.evidence: SPARK_MILESTONES.md S10 (big-core split: 100 MHz OAI 1x1 1,424-1,506 -> 1,995-2,077 slots/s) and S11 (broker 2 -> 3 cores: emulator-call p99 115-135 -> 65 us at 100 MHz, CPU and CUDA gNB, real time kept; UE on 1 core or on little cores falls below real time)
spark-gb10.broker_env_evidence: SPARK_MILESTONES.md S15 (OAI 2x2, broker pinned to 15-17: spinning broker waits on top of the in-place relay raise 100 MHz idle 0.620/0.616 (fewer copies alone) -> 0.670-0.686 and 50 MHz idle 0.866 -> 0.996; costs the three broker cores at 100%)
spark-gb10.gnb_env_evidence: X6 (docs/plans/x6-gnb-realtime-traffic.md): OCUDU sizes its main worker pool min(5, pinned_cpus-3), so the 5-core gNB pin leaves 2 workers; in ZMQ mode every DU-high cell executor is a sync strand over that pool and two UEs in iperf UL exhaust it (gdb: phy_worker + both workers in sync waits, run 20261001T115125Z wedged at UL+32 s; Track D runs likewise). nof_threads 5 = the unpinned default; run 20261001T120308Z held 200 s at 20 Mbit/s UL with no stall. Exported only when the caller has not set it; the renderer writes expert_execution.threads.main_pool.nof_threads.
spark-gb10.gnb_lower_phy_note: X6: all ten big cores are allocated (gNB 5, broker 3, UE 2), so a non-sequential lower-PHY profile gets no extra big core -- moot on a1916edc, whose zmq driver forces the sequential profile. The gNB's 5 cores hold the sequential phy_worker plus radio/du_high/io threads; dual would add 2 and triple 3 RT threads, which still fit in 5-9. Taking cores from the broker (S11: 3 needed) or the UEs (S11: 1 core falls below real time) is not worth it; little cores 0-4,10-14 are left out on purpose (the why above). Override per run with OCUDU_NATIVE_GNB_CPUS.

jetson-orin-30w.evidence: JETSON_MILESTONES.md J8 (AGX Orin MODE_30W, 8 of 12 A78AE cores online, OAI 1x1 20 MHz: unpinned 580-600 slots/s (0.58-0.60x) -> gNB 0-4 / UE 5 / broker 6-7 806-811 slots/s (0.81x), broker p99 895-1025 -> 575-590 us; a gNB confined to 4 cores never starts its radio)
